100% must try. Worth of a daily breakfast.
Nov 2025 • Family
A beautiful place right in the area of the peacepalace. Sitting on the outside border of the beautifully maintained park.

You better be here by 8 in the morning because otherwise you wont be able to get their signature breakfast dish. A perch noodle soup with lots of dill. A Taste that reminds you of europe. With the dish comes a complimentary tea that is harvested in northern vietnam. Usually it containes as much caffeine as the coffee so its watered down and served with ice.

What a Taste. You need to give it a try. Sadly today i was to slow and arrived close to 10ish. The soup was sold out as usual so i had the pho. While also really good, nothing compares to the "ca ro".

Poor food
Oct 2019 • Couples
This is a tempting spot on the edge of a green park, but don’t judge the book by its cover. We arrived at 1200 and asked for two banh mi. Eventually the waitress returned to tell us they only had one bread loaf left. OK. We’ll just have one, with tuna. When the tuna arrived it was tinned sardines. We refused it and were eventually offered a substitute and chose pate. Some time later, a scant tablespoon of pate arrived - no salad, no pickles, none of the usual accompaniments. So our option was a bread roll with a smear of pate. I’m sure there was some miscommunication going on, but also inefficiency and a lack of interest in customers. We noticed as we left that none of the Vietnamese customers were eating. Perhaps a place for a drink, but I would advise you to follow their lead.

They do make an effort
Jan 2019 • Solo
Had a walk around the Independence Palace and came across this cafe. Decided to give it a try. The heat had been relentless and I was a little peckish.

Ordered a simple pho and sour plum sida water. Am impressed they make an effort here with a full bamboo tray of condiments to go with the noodles, and a separate serving of ice, and sour plum in its juice to go with the soda water rather then just mix it all together to save a bit of washing up.

The pho was ok, not outstanding but the cafe is spacious and offers shade in a large open spave.

Good Food and service but watch the bill
Sep 2018 • Couples
This is a nice cafe / restaurant within the grounds of the Independence Palace - the only venue of the three that I saw that serves food.
The menu covers the usual Vietnamese dishes and reasonably priced, considering that it is located within a major tourist attraction. Definitely comparable to restaurants outside, but more expensive than the street vendors.
A lovely lady served us and was very patience with us, as we pointed out our choices on the menu and ordered coffee (probably pronouncing the words badly)
The restaurant was very busy as it was lunch time and everyone was waiting for 1pm when the Independence Palace opens to the public. Food arrived quickly, though the drinks were a bit longer. The food was vey tasty and as it arrived, so did the tropical downpour. The staff were quick to move people further inside to stop them getting wet.

The only negative came was when the bill arrived, delivered by a different, younger lady. All nicely printed and it matched what we were expecting except for one item - we were charged for 5 of something. We hadn't had 5 of anything, so Google translate was used to show we were being charged for 5 cold towels. Cold towels are a chargeable item if you use them in many restaurants, so no surprise for it to be included. Except that we had only been given 2 and not used them. Since 2 and 5 are next to each other on the keyboard, I assumed a simple mistake. 
Its what happened next, that makes me think it was not - we were the only non locals in the cafe at this point. My traveling companion brought the item to the attention of the young lady, who scowled and quickly gave us the correct cost. We gave her the money for the meal - when the change returned, she disappeared immediately. The change was all in VDN 5,000 and 1,000 notes - when it could easily have been in VDN 20,000 or VDN50,000. It was the correct amount of change but there was no need for the pettiness. This was probably the only time on the whole trip we experienced such behaviour. 
We usually leave a tip in cash as we leave but it looks like one or more of the staff had decided to pre-empt and include it in the bill, removing our choice.
